headlines.text: That Sunday in 2022, Jon Moxley vs. Hiroshi Tanahashi etched their names into history in the first-ever AEW Interim World Title match, appearing on Forbidden Door, rated 8.08 ? an excellent showing. This first-ever singles meeting closed the show with Moxley putting Tanahashi through the timekeeper's table before locking in the Death Rider to become interim AEW World Champion.

Flash back to 2021, when the AEW World Heavyweight Title was up for grabs as Kenny Omega vs. Jungle Boy went to war, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.43 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. A coming-of-age moment for the young star ? Jungle Boy earned his shot by eliminating Christian Cage from a Casino Battle Royale, and gave the champion a real scare, nearly forcing him to submit before outside interference saved the title reign.
Rewind to 2024, when Hiromu Takahashi arrived in AEW, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.15.

secondaries.text: Rewind to 2022, when a new chapter began as PAC vs. Clark Connors vs. Malakai Black vs. Miro fought for the brand-new AEW All-Atlantic Title, appearing on Forbidden Door, rated 7.74 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. Connors, a late replacement for the injured Tomohiro Ishii, won over the Chicago crowd by spearing Miro through a table, but it was PAC who submitted him to become the first-ever All-Atlantic Champion.

Looking back to 2022, when Will Ospreay vs. Orange Cassidy fought tooth and nail for the IWGP United States Title, appearing on Forbidden Door, rated 9.04 ? a match fans still talk about. It was the first title opportunity of Will Ospreay's career. Cassidy's laid-back style threw Ospreay off from the opening bell, and after a string of near-falls this one stole the show ? capped by a surprise Katsuyori Shibata debut chasing off the post-match beatdown.

Turning the clock back to 2022: history was made as Jay White vs. Adam Page vs. Adam Cole vs. Kazuchika Okada contested the very first IWGP World Heavyweight Title match, appearing on Forbidden Door, rated 7.45 ? a good, competitive contest. White and Cole briefly worked together as Bullet Club allies before White turned on his own partner, sneaking in a Blade Runner to steal the pin on Cole and retain the title.
